original_quote: The check ... to prevent path traversal doesn't account for subdirectories inside the temp folder. (affects gradio 4.0-4.10; /file endpoint arbitrary file read)
bypass_quote: The is_in_or_equal function may be bypassed. Affected versions are vulnerable to Directory Traversal ... An attacker can access restricted files by manipulating file paths using parent directory sequences (..). Ensure that all file paths are properly resolved and absolute.

sink_evolution.v0_4.10.0: if str(path_1.relative_to(path_2)).startswith('..'): return False   # subdir-prefixed relative path does NOT start with '..' -> escapes
sink_evolution.v1_4.11.0: if '..' in str(path_1.relative_to(path_2)): return False           # CVE-2023-51449 fix: catches literal '..' anywhere; abspath() still never resolves symlinks
sink_evolution.v2_5.0.0: path_1, path_2 = abspath(path_1).resolve(), abspath(path_2).resolve(); path_1.relative_to(path_2)  # CVE-2024-47164 fix: normalizes '..' AND resolves symlinks

residual_mechanism: Pure lexical '..' is caught by V1's substring check, so the genuine residual that survives V1 but dies at V2's .resolve() is a SYMLINK bypass: abspath() explicitly does not resolve symlinks (and returns absolute inputs un-normalized), so a symlink inside the allowed dir yields a relative path with no '..' -> is_in_or_equal True on V1 -> FileResponse follows the symlink out of the allowed dir. V2's added .resolve() collapses the symlink and closes it. Same is_in_or_equal containment sink, hardened across two releases.
note: The advisory frames CVE-2024-47164 as '.. sequences'; the actual code fix is `.resolve()` ('ensure paths are properly resolved and absolute'), which is precisely symlink+`..` normalization. Empirically, a literal `..`-only payload is blocked by 4.11.0, so the residual demonstrated here is the symlink form that 4.11.0's substring guard misses.
